BASAVARAJA, J., DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT
This appeal is filed by the appellant/claimant challenging the judgment and award dated 02nd April 2016 passed in MVC No.1472 of 2014 by the Court of IX Addl.
District and Sessions Judge and Member Addl. MACT, Belagavi (for short hereinafter referred to as the "Tribunal") seeking enhancement of compensation.
2. For the sake of convenience, the parties in this appeal are referred to as per their status and rank before the Tribunal.

3. Brief facts of the case are that:
On 07.09.2013 at about 9.00 am the petitioner was standing by the side of the bus stand in order to board the bus bearing No.KA-22/F-1778 and when the petitioner was trying to board the bus, the driver suddenly moved the bus in a rash and negligent manner and the petitioner fell on the road, the bus ran over his leg and he sustained grievous injuries.
The petitioner took treatment at two different hospitals in Belagavi NC: 2023:KHC-D:10648-DB i.e. BIMS Hospital, and Kapileshwar Hospital by spending a sum of Rs.1,25,000/-.
He was under bed rest for a period of three months and was an inpatient from 07th September to 05th October 2013.
The petitioner was aged about 28 years and was earning a sum of Rs.400/- per day by doing mason work.
On all these grounds, the claimant has preferred claim petition seeking compensation.
4. Pursuant to notice respondent appeared and filed objection denying the petition averments.
It is contended that the petitioner is himself responsible for the accident and accordingly sought for dismissal of the claim petition.

5. Based on the rival pleadings, the Tribunal has framed the following issues:

sentences.text: Whether the petitioner proves that due to the rash and negligent driving of the Bus bearing No.KA- 22/F-1778 by its driver, the accident happened and in the said accident he has sustained grievous injuries?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, what is the quantum and from whom?
3 . What order or award?
In order to prove his case, the claimant himself examined as PW1 and examined Doctor as PW2 and got marked 12 documents as per Exhibits P1 to P12.
Respondent has not adduced any evidence on its part.

7. Upon hearing the arguments of the learned counsel for the parties, the Tribunal has answered the issues as under:
 Issue No.1: In the affirmative.
Issue No.2: In the affirmative.
Issue No.3: As per final order, for the following;

8. In view of the above finding, the Tribunal allowed the petition in part and awarded compensation of Rs.2,41,200/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realisation.
Being not satisfied with the compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the claimant is before this Court seeking enhancement of compensation.
9. We have heard the learned counsel appearing for the parties.

10. Learned counsel appearing for the appellant-claimant submits that the Tribunal has not considered that the appellant has suffered injuries like fracture of lower 1/3rd right fibula, fracture of posterior right tibia, degloving injury of right leg and exterior tendon injury which affect the extremities and limbs.
He submits that the Tribunal has not considered the functional disability at 100%.
PW2-Doctor has assessed the disability at 35%.
He further submits that Tribunal has not awarded just compensation on all other heads and accordingly sought for enhancement in compensation.

11. On the other hand, the learned counsel appearing for the respondent-NWKRTC supports the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal and submits that the Tribunal, after considering the oral and documentary evidence on record, has awarded just compensation and the same does not call for interference in this appeal and hence prays for dismissal of the appeal.

3 12. Having heard the learned counsel for the parties, the following questions would arise for our consideration in this appeal:
1.

Whether the appellant/claimant is entitled for enhancement of compensation as sought for:
2. What order of award?

13. Our answer for the above points are as under:
Point No.1: partly in the affirmative; Point No.2: As per final order NC:
2023:KHC-D:10648-DB Regarding Point No.1:
14.
The accident is not in dispute and the claimant suffering injuries in the accident is also not in dispute.
PW1- petitioner has deposed in his evidence as to the wounds/fractures sustained by him and also with regard to taking treatment as an inpatient and as to his permanent disability.
He has also examined the Doctor as PW2 has deposed that the petitioner has suffered 35% permanent physical disability in relation to right lower limb.
Petitioner also produced Exhibit P5-wound certificate.
Exhibit P7-discharge card of BIMS Hospital, Belgaum and Exhibit P8-Radiology report and Exhibit P9-X ray and Exhibits P10 and P11 x-rays films.
Considering the nature of injuries/fracture and medical evidence, it is just and proper to assess the disability of the petitioner at 15% to the whole body.
The petitioner, as on the date of accident, was aged 25 years.
Since the income is not proved by providing documents, it is appropriate to take the notional income as per the guidelines issued by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.

According to the guidelines,
for the accidents of the year 2013, the notional income is Rs.7,000/- and the same is taken in this case also.

Then the NC: 2023:KHC-D:10648-DB loss of future income comes to Rs.2,26,800/-
(Rs.7,000/- x 12 x 18 x 15%).

Considering the nature of injury, pain and suffering of the claimant, it is just and proper to award compensation as under:
Amount Sl.No. Heads (in Rs.)
1 Pain and suffering 50,000.00
Food, Nourishment and attendant 2 30,000.00 charges 3 Loss of earning during treatment 21,000.00 4 Loss of amenities 30,000.00 5
Loss of future earning 2,26,800.00
Accordingly, the point No.1 is answered in the affirmative.
